newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea seen preparing for peace talks - Seoul.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea seen preparing for peace talks - Seoul.

text.p: North Korea is expected to agree to a meeting of senior officials from the United States and South Korea to arrange four-nation peace talks, a South Korean foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.

Spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung told Reuters that progress had been made in working-level discussions among the three countries in New York recently and South Korea was "cautiously optimistic" over the prospects of holding peace talks this year.
The four-nation talks, also involving China, are aimed at working out a peace settlement to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
China has said it will join the four-way talks once the three other nations agree on a formula for the negotiations.
Lee said officials from the United States and the two Koreas had met five times since May 30. "There's been slow but positive progress," he added. No details were given.
He said he expected senior officials of the three countries to meet "within the next couple of months" to discuss the agenda and other procedural details for the four-nation talks.
"Before the preparatory talks, an assistant minister-level meeting is expected in New York among the three countries to formally launch the process," he said.

In a similar meeting in New York last April, famine-threatened North Korea agreed in principle to join four-nation peace talks but made its participation conditional on large-scale food aid and an easing of U.S. trade sanctions.
South Korea and the United States have said such assistance could be discussed during peace talks.

Washington and Seoul say humanitarian assistance would be provided to help stave off a catastrophe but Pyongyang must not be allowed to use participation in the four-way talks as leverage to extract food assistance.
The United States has pledged $25 million and South Korea $16 million in response to the U.N. World Food Programme's appeal for 203,000 tonnes of food for North Korea.
Last Thursday, the South Korean Red Cross started delivering 11,200 tonnes of corn to North Korea via China.
The corn is the first of 50,000 tonnes of food the South Korean Red Cross has pledged to supply to the North by the end of July.
A group of South Korean civic groups has promised to donate a further 30,000 tonnes of corn to North Korea.
